introduction: Recover Bone Fort Inn’s four stolen books, follow the snowy boots to Eleadora, help the hungry village and deliver foreign materials to its shaman. Keep exact item kinds, optional supply routes, two different keys and Eleadora’s departure visible while exploring the tundra.
orientation: Bone Fort Inn’s hunched man accepts four different books together for snowy adventurer boots. Eleadora accepts those exact boots for glowing ice leggings and independently accepts Malinar’s bloody head for the tundra sword. The shaman’s fire gland and shell requests are two independent outcomes; feeding the barbarian needs three different seafood kinds together.

Follow the Surface highway entrance into Bone Fort Inn, open the northern bone door and go west into reception. The stairs north of the lobby go down to the Onyx Stairs. Western bedrooms hold the old, magenta and green books on different travellers; the dark traveller near the entrance holds the black book. Other copies of those guests begin without books.

The northern door at the Onyx Stairs is visible and closed despite the secret-passage description. Open it to reach the passages behind the rooms. Bedroom back doors are generally secret through their resets. In the shady traveller’s bedroom, PUSH the working mirror to open the blocked north passage; the mirrors described in other bedrooms are scenery.

Below the passage’s grate is the underground river, with sharks and an actual water sector. The dragon may emerge into the fire-beaten cave after its loading branch; it is not guaranteed to appear. Red scales support the blacksmith’s paid service. Open the Ice Lounge’s visible closed southern door to Ixarvonl’s workshop; SEARCH is not required and no research or invasion outcome is bound.

Eleadora and Malinar may emerge into the forest or tundra, or become inaccessible in loading branches. Find the actual actor when present. Return the snowy adventurer boots before giving Eleadora the head if you want both rewards in the same encounter: she leaves after the head exchange. These are independent receipts, without a forced boots-before-head requirement.

Feed the starving barbarian a small clam, a large pike and an impressive lobster together. His fishbone key unlocks the western flap to the shaman’s home and breaks on ordinary successful unlocking. That reward and the shaman’s later fire gland or shell receipts remain separate; public access or supplied items do not require personal feeding history.

FISH requires fishing skill, a recognised pole and a usable water room. The village’s Fishing Docks are coded as land; the name alone does not make FISH work there. The inn’s underground river is water but hazardous. Bom Fitherwood in Harrow trades a painting for a pike, lobster and hairy crab: you still need a clam. Foreign paid fish purchases remain unavailable while accounting is active.

The snapjaw turtle shell and fire gland come from foreign loaded creatures. Ship-yard dispersal sources and the Crimson Fulgur provide both kinds; Alatorin bladeback pyrolisks provide fire glands. Remove a worn shell or gland before offering it. Supplying either exact item is valid without your own kill, source journey or earlier feeding receipt.

The wife’s small wooden key fits the separate locked northern flap to the fishmonger’s hut and breaks on ordinary successful unlocking. It does not replace the fishbone key. The wife’s complaint is ambient; the fishmonger has no configured shop, so do not rely on him to supply the seafood.

The general store sells rations, water, a backpack, potions and bandages. Iron rations support a different foreign Cairme exchange and do not satisfy the starving barbarian. The blacksmith’s scales AND 500-platinum service remains unavailable with active accounting and earns no zone achievement or daily credit.

Some crossing signs describe routes absent from the loaded exits. The southern mountain pass has no usable southern destination, and an eastern forest exit points to an inactive legacy map room. Use verified Surface entrances; the journal does not promise those unresolved routes or send you into loading rooms.

Carry exact materials loose. Worn, nested, spent or handed-away copies remain missing; earlier receipts never replace them. Questions and source recovery explain progress without granting every keyword an achievement. Only accepted exact exchanges record outcomes. All new discovery, encounter, journal, achievement and daily credit requires active, ready accounting; frozen reward recovery remains separate.

contacts.name: a hunched man
contacts.description: At the reception library of Bone Fort Inn. Ask about hi, books, guests and boots. He needs all four different books together; the bookrack is not their source.

contacts.name: a barbarian blacksmith
contacts.description: In the village blacksmith’s hut, east of the village path. Ask about hi, scales or dragon. His red-scales AND 500-platinum order is currently unavailable with active accounting.

contacts.name: Eleadora, guardian of the ice forest
contacts.description: May emerge from a branching loading route into the ice forest. Ask about hi, boots or boot, malinar and sword. Her boots and head exchanges are independent; she leaves after the head exchange.

contacts.name: a barbarian shaman
contacts.description: In the fisherman’s home behind the locked western flap near the starving barbarian. Ask hi. A fishbone key from feeding the barbarian opens the flap and breaks on ordinary successful unlocking. Exact supplied materials do not require an earlier feeding receipt.

contacts.name: a starving barbarian
contacts.description: At the bend beside the locked western flap to the shaman’s home. Ask hi, hello or hey. Needs a clam AND pike AND lobster together; gives the fishbone key.

contacts.name: a strange guest
contacts.description: Two strange-looking guests begin in inn bedrooms. Only the one in the far western bedroom starts carrying the hidden dark green book.

contacts.name: a shady traveller
contacts.description: Two shady travellers begin in inn bedrooms. Only the one with the working mirror starts carrying the hidden dark magenta book. PUSH that mirror opens the blocked northern passage.

contacts.name: a human traveller
contacts.description: Two human travellers begin in inn bedrooms. Only the one in the western bedroom nearest the stairs starts carrying the old book.

contacts.name: a dark traveller
contacts.description: At the inn entrance, starts carrying the hidden dark black book. Other travellers and duplicate guests do not substitute for this fourth kind.

contacts.name: a thundering red dragon
contacts.description: May reach the fire-beaten cave below the inn through its loading route. Starts carrying hidden red dragon scales. Scales recovery, personal victory and paid armor preparation are different facts.

contacts.name: Malinar, blood enemy of Eleadora
contacts.description: May emerge into the icy tundra from branching loading rooms. Starts with his own exact bloody head already carried. His rare grey giant boots do not satisfy Eleadora’s snowy adventurer boots request.

contacts.name: an angry barbarian wife
contacts.description: At the end of the village path beside the locked northern flap to the fishmonger’s hut. Carries the hidden small wooden key. Her qc_action80 complaint is ambient dialogue, not an asked keyword or separate quest.

contacts.name: a barbarian fishmonger
contacts.description: In the fisherman’s hut behind the locked northern flap. The wife’s wooden key fits that flap and breaks on ordinary successful unlocking. His selling prose has no configured shop binding or accepted exchange.

contacts.name: a barbarian-human halfbreed
contacts.description: At the small general store reached from the snowy crossing or the Surface highway. Sells rations, water, a backpack, potions and bandages. Rations do not replace the three required seafood kinds.

contacts.name: Ixarvonl, the great illithid alchemist
contacts.description: May reach the ancient workshop behind the Ice Lounge’s visible closed southern door through a loading route. His invasion plans and laboratory are context; no local accepted invasion or research quest is bound.

contacts.name: a pale bartender
contacts.description: At the Ice Lounge below the Onyx Stairs. Open the visible closed southern door to the ancient workshop. The bartender has no configured shop or accepted exchange.

stories.title: Bone Fort Inn: return four different books
stories.summary: Return the old, dark green, dark magenta and dark black books together to the hunched man for a pair of snowy adventurer boots. Four copies of one book do not substitute. His thanks mention killing the thieves, but the exchange accepts the four exact books without requiring your own kills.

steps.hint: One human traveller begins in the western bedroom closest to the stairs with this book. The other human traveller in a farther bedroom starts without it. Carry the exact item loose; worn, nested, spent and handed-away copies do not count. Supplied copies need no personal source kill or catch.

One strange-looking guest begins in the far western bedroom with this book. Another guest in a different bedroom starts without it. Carry the exact item loose; worn, nested, spent and handed-away copies do not count. Supplied copies need no personal source kill or catch.

One shady traveller begins in the western bedroom with the working mirror and carries this book. Another shady traveller farther east starts without it. Carry the exact item loose; worn, nested, spent and handed-away copies do not count. Supplied copies need no personal source kill or catch.
